correctness.rationale: For a primitive degree-\(d\) core, its roots are \(\alpha,\alpha^Q,\ldots,\alpha^{Q^{d-1}}\), so the focal source's exterior-product formula gives modes \((-1)^k\alpha^{E_I}\) with \(E_I=\sum_{i\in I}Q^i\). For \(1\le k<d\), these subset exponents are distinct integers strictly between 0 and \(Q^d-1\), hence distinct modulo the order of primitive \(\alpha\). Frobenius multiplication of the exponent by Q rotates the binary support, so minimal-polynomial orbits are exactly cyclic-rotation orbits. A word with orbit size \(d/h\) is an h-fold repetition and forces \(h\mid k\); Möbius inversion gives the stated primitive-necklace count. The coprime case and the irreducibility boundary follow immediately. An independent enumeration reproduced the necklace degree formula for all \(2\le d\le10\), \(1\le k<d\).
